title: Rick & Morty Explore the First Programming Languages!
caption: Ever wonder who started coding? #ProgrammingHistory

scenes.script: Hey Rick! I just read that Ada Lovelace created the first machine algorithm in 1843. How did she do that without a computer?

Oh, Morty! Ada was way ahead of her time. She realized numbers could represent other things—like music or text. Basically, she invented the concept of a computer program before computers even existed!
So... she was like the grandma of programming? That’s kinda cool.
Exactly! Now, the first actual programming language for computers was Plankalkül by Konrad Zuse in the 1940s. It helped engineers do repetitive tasks—like building a spaceship, Morty!
Wait, so if Ada was the grandma, Zuse was the dad of programming?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

scenes.script: Ha! You got it. Later came Assembly Language and Shortcode in 1949, which were like the first real coding tools—still used today for low-level stuff.
Like... building a portal gun? That’s important, Rick!
Exactly! And then FORTRAN in 1957—still used for science and engineering today. It’s the grandpa of modern languages, Morty!
So, FORTRAN is like a dinosaur that’s still alive? That’s crazy.
Yep! And ALGOL in 1958 set the stage for Pascal, Java, C—pretty much everything we use now. It was like the blueprint for modern programming.
So... if you want to build a new universe, you should start with ALGOL? Got it, Rick!
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: You’re learning, Morty! Remember: coding is like a portal—you can create anything with the right language. Now go write some code!

topic: What was the first programming language?
